expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: CLAUDE.md is a memory aid, not an enforcement layer; A ~1-in-10 violation rate is roughly what you'd expect from instruction-following alone

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: The fix is to move both rules out of text and into something the harness enforces before the tool call runs

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: Force-push needs a hook, not a deny pattern. A string-prefix deny won't catch git push origin main --force

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: A bare denied gets the agent creatively working around it; The message above names what was blocked and what to do instead

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: Try an actual force-push and an actual edit and confirm both the denial and the message fire; then confirm an ordinary push and ordinary edit elsewhere still work

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: Put this in .claude/settings.json and commit it, not settings.local.json. Local-only protection is the same failure mode

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: it's not going to converge to 0 by adding a third exclamation point
